transcript.content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Hi, one of our Hosted API usage lines looks higher than we expected. What did it cost, and why might it be higher? Org is acme-analytics.

{"name": "usage-and-metering", "steps": "Goal: explain the developer's numbers from console records and current policy, and hand off only what the policy pages can't explain.

1. Get the facts. If not given, ask_developer once for what you need: ["org_id", "request_ids", "response_status", "error_code", "time_of_issue", "timezone", "billing_period", "checks_done"]. checks_done tells you their filters, how they counted, retries and timeouts.
2. Look up the account (note plan and billing_timezone), then get_usage for the request ids (or the invoice line). Read http_status, billed_tokens, cached_tokens, time in UTC and in the billing timezone, and billed_on_line. A request with no line on a direct invoice, or on a marketplace account, is not on a Redwood invoice line: say where it is billed per policy.
3. search_knowledge for the explanation, e.g. ["API error reference 402 quota_exceeded 429 rate limited", "how billed tokens are counted cache hits", "retries and streaming cancellation billing", "invoice periods billing timezone late usage prior-period", "usage missing from console threshold hourly batch", "embeddings batch usage delay"]. Use the current page when two disagree (e.g. an older free-tier page vs the newer error reference) and say which is current.
4. Compare their count to the explanation: billing month cut in the account's billing timezone (for the periods the close calendar says) vs their timezone, late usage billed next month as prior-period usage, project filters, prompt-only counting, client retries/timeouts, cancelled streams, tool-call payload, cache hits. Name the cause that fits their facts.
5. Decide:
   - Explained by a policy page: explain with their own numbers; no case, even if they call it a bug or double billing.
   - Still unexplained after those rules for specific request ids: route per the routing table (load billing-handoff) with the ids and what you checked.
   - Successful requests missing from the Console: compare the time since the request with the threshold the routing page gives for that request's date (and the endpoint's own delay page); before it, explain and say when to check again, no case; after it, route per policy.
   - Quota vs rate-limit errors: answer what the error means for their plan and when it clears, per the error reference and packages page.
   - They want correctly billed usage removed or credited: that's a credit/exception request; route per policy.
6. Reply with the answer first, then the detail and what they can change, quoting console figures."}

Tickets, email and chat are history unless a published page adopts them.", "results": [{"chunk_id": "d18494816f6272ef", "source": "confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/usage-accounting-retries-and-stream-cancellation", "title": "Usage accounting: retries and streaming cancellation", "status": "published", "updated": "2025-02-18", "section": "content > Overview | content > Key definitions | content > Retries", "text": "[content > Overview]
Some customers reconcile Redwood token usage against internal estimates and may observe higher usage totals. The most common causes are (1) client retries and (2) streaming cancellation behavior.

This page provides a support-ready explanation and recommended mitigations.

[content > Key definitions]
- **Attempt**: a single request admitted by the Redwood API gateway (server-side).
- **Logical request**: what the customer thinks of as one user action; may map to multiple attempts if the client retries.

[content > Retries]
- Redwood usage is recorded per-attempt.
- If a client retries after a timeout or non-200 response, each admitted attempt can be billable.
- The Usage dashboard lists rows by **request_id** (attempt identifier)."}, {"chunk_id": "579f2a01b1537562", "source": "confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/hosted-api-packages-free-tier-and-overage-policy", "title": "Hosted API Packages: Free Tier, Included Usage, and Overage Policy", "status": "published", "updated": "2026-02-26", "section": "content > Principles | content > Approved phrases (use these)", "text": "[content > Principles]

- Emphasize predictability and transparency.

- **Prompt tokens** are counted once the request is admitted (even if the client cancels the stream later).
- **Completion tokens** are counted based on tokens actually generated/streamed prior to cancellation.

[content > Common customer symptoms]
- We only sent N requests but we see >N rows: retries created additional attempts.
- We timed out at 15s so we expected zero bill: prompt tokens + partial completion tokens may still be counted.

[content > Recommended mitigations]
1) Avoid automatic retries on client-side timeouts for long generations.
2) Increase client timeout where possible (align to max expected generation time).
3) Reduce max_tokens / output length to meet latency budgets.
4) For troubleshooting, ask for a small set of request_ids + the customers retry/cancel metrics."}, {"chunk_id": "6a5f65a250b6fd9d", "source": "confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/hosted-api-packages-free-tier-and-overage-policy", "title": "Hosted API Packages: Free Tier, Included Usage, and Overage Policy", "status": "published", "updated": "2026-02-26", "section": "content > What “included usage” means | content > Billing period | content > Canonical Hosted API package policy (standard self-serve)", "text": "[content > What “included usage” means]
Included usage is the amount bundled with a package **during a billing period**. Charges apply only when:
1) a customer is on a plan that allows overage, and

1) Start a streaming generation request with a high token budget (e.g., max_tokens=2048) and capture the session id from the gateway logs.
2) Interrupt the TCP connection mid-stream (simulate flaky network).

The Hosted API line for **Aug 1–15** on invoice **INV-BG-202608-009** is **$1,301.46**. The invoice is currently open. The line covers three requests, totaling **41,565,393 billed tokens**; all three show HTTP 200 in the usage records.

Your client retries after 10-second timeouts could explain higher usage: Redwood records usage per admitted attempt, so a retry can be billed separately, and a client timeout doesn’t necessarily mean the original attempt stopped before generating billable tokens. The records don’t show whether these three requests were retries, so I can’t confirm that was the cause. There’s no contract on file in the console; cached tokens are shown separately and don’t reduce billed totals unless a contract explicitly provides a discount.
So retries are billed as usage too?

Yes—**a retry can be billed** if it reaches Redwood and is admitted as a separate attempt. Usage is recorded per attempt, based on billed tokens processed; a timeout doesn’t necessarily mean the original attempt stopped before generating billable usage. Not every retry is automatically billed: a request that fails before inference begins may have no reported usage.
